proto.help.p1: Pick a game and a layout in the top bar, then click a window on the board. The inspector shows its position, scale, opacity and section switches. The preview draws demo data — editing here never touches a running game.
proto.help.p2: With a window selected, choose the screen it should appear on under Target display. Following the main panel reuses that panel's screen; if the panel has none, the primary screen is used. The top-bar Display selector only changes the board you are looking at — it never changes a window's ownership.
proto.help.p3: Whole draws each panel as one window; Split carves it into small windows; Mixed lets you choose, window by window, whether it stays separate or merges back into its main panel. Each game and layout keeps its own position and size, so switching layouts does not overwrite the other set.
proto.help.p4: Changes are written when you close the console (panels.ini and monster-overlay.conf), and the console saves first if you launch the overlay without closing — there is no manual Save. Export writes the current set to text for backup or comparison; it is not the config file. Reset Layout restores the current group to the shipped default; Reset All covers both games and all three layouts.
proto.help.p5: Edit layout moves windows on the console board only. Edit in overlay launches the real overlay so you can drag windows over the game; closing it saves and returns you to the console; arrow keys move 1px, Shift+arrows 10px, Esc leaves edit mode.

Values in the panels and the preview are demo data; “is a process attached” comes from real detection. Closing the console (or launching the overlay) writes the configuration for the selected game × layout scope, and the overlay starts reading live data once it is launched.
